articles.title: Magic news: Sean Sweeney reveals major offensive emphasis for 2026-27
articles.summary: Orlando Magic head coach Sean Sweeney is placing a major emphasis on spacing as he begins installing his offensive system ahead of the 2026-27 NBA season. Th...
articles.body:
Orlando Magic head coach Sean Sweeney is placing a major emphasis on spacing as he begins installing his offensive system ahead of the 2026-27 NBA season.

The Magic wrapped up their second day of training camp Wednesday as Sweeney continued introducing his approach to a roster led by Paolo Banchero, Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane. Speaking with Ryan Kaminski of Orlando Magic on SI NBA, Sweeney explained how Orlando intends to stretch opposing defenses by utilizing the entire floor.

"We would rather be too high, too wide, too far apart, too spaced," Sweeney said. "There's different times where you may want four out, one in. There's different times when you want five out but in general, with the way we run, we want to do a great job with our spacing and make the defense guard the length and width of the court."

Sweeney's emphasis on spacing comes as the Magic attempt to take another step offensively after showing improvement last season. Orlando's offense climbed from 27th in the NBA to 18th during the 2025-26 regular season, but its perimeter shooting remained an area in need of improvement.

The Magic ranked 27th in 3-point shooting and encountered additional offensive struggles during their first-round playoff series against the Detroit Pistons . Orlando averaged a playoff-low 97.7 points per game during the seven-game series.

Sean Sweeney looking to reshape Magic offense for 2026-27

Spacing represents one part of Sweeney's broader offensive philosophy.

The first-year Magic coach previously said he wants Orlando to play with an aggressive but disciplined approach, pushing the ball up the floor while creating opportunities through passing and screening.

Sweeney's system could provide Banchero and Wagner with additional room to attack while also creating perimeter opportunities for Bane and Orlando's supporting cast. Maintaining proper spacing could become particularly important when the Magic use five-out lineups designed to pull opposing defenders away from the paint.

Orlando's training camp provides Sweeney with his first opportunity to implement those principles in a full team setting.

With the Magic looking to move beyond three consecutive first-round playoff exits, developing a more efficient offense will be among the team's priorities throughout training camp and into Sweeney's first season as head coach.

articles.title: HISTORY MADE: Caitlin Clark Does What No WNBA Player Has Done to Save Fever
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark entered Game 2 with the Indiana Fever facing the end of their season. Las Vegas had taken control of the series, and Indiana needed a much bett...
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark entered Game 2 with the Indiana Fever facing the end of their season. Las Vegas had taken control of the series, and Indiana needed a much better performance Tuesday at Gainbridge Fieldhouse.

The Fever had struggled throughout Game 1. They committed 17 turnovers and allowed the Aces to shoot 59.4% from the field in a 102-85 loss.

Caitlin Clark Makes WNBA History As Fever Force Game 3

Clark gave Indiana the response it needed. The Fever beat the Aces 99-89 on Tuesday to tie the best-of-three series. The teams will now return to Las Vegas for a deciding Game 3.

Clark finished with 27 points, 15 assists and seven rebounds. She made nine of her 18 shots, including five of 11 three-point attempts.

The performance made Clark the first player in WNBA history to score at least 25 points and record 15 assists in one game.

Clark's scoring and assists created 58 of Indiana's 99 points. According to CBS Sports, that tied the league record for the most points created by one player in a playoff game. Her 15 assists were also the third-most in a playoff game in WNBA history.

However, the game did not start smoothly for Clark. She had five turnovers in the first half and received a technical foul after arguing a call early in the second quarter.

Clark settled down after halftime and did not commit another turnover.

"I thought we were just soft in Game 1 and I thought tonight we played much tougher," Clark said after the game.

That tougher play was clear late in the game. Clark made back-to-back three-pointers in the fourth quarter. The second was a 30-foot step-back shot over A'ja Wilson that helped Indiana rebuild its lead after Las Vegas had cut the gap.

Caitlin Clark Gets Help As Fever Survive Aces Push

Clark did not carry the Fever alone. Kelsey Mitchell scored 26 points, while Aliyah Boston added 22 points, four rebounds and five assists.

Clark, Mitchell and Boston combined for 75 of Indiana's 99 points. That means the three players scored more than three-quarters of the team's total.

Their support became even more important after Clark fouled out with 2:45 remaining. Las Vegas cut Indiana's lead to five points, but Boston answered with a basket. Mitchell then helped finish the game at the free-throw line.

The win changed the direction of the series after Las Vegas controlled Game 1. Wilson had 38 points and 16 rebounds in the opener.

Wilson led the Aces again in Game 2 with 22 points and nine rebounds. Jackie Young scored a team-high 31 points.

Clark now enters the deciding game after averaging 22.3 points and 8.3 assists during the regular season. She was also named AP Comeback Player of the Year and made the AP All-WNBA First Team after missing most of the previous season.

Indiana needed a major response after Game 1. Clark delivered it, and the Fever now have one more game to keep their season alive.

articles.title: Michael Jordan's Custom Ferrari 550 Maranello Sells for $2.7M at Auction
articles.summary: A car once owned by an NBA legend sold for a massive price at auction on Wednesday.
articles.body:
A car once owned by an NBA legend sold for a massive price at auction on Wednesday.

Michael Jordan's custom Ferrari 550 Maranello sold at Joopiter Auctions for $2.7 million. According to Joopiter, the vehicle was rediscovered this year after 24 years out of the public eye.

Jordan purchased the car in May of 1997 and was seen leaving the United Center hours after winning his fifth NBA championship with the Chicago Bulls. According to Joopiter, Jordan had a cigar in his hand and the Larry O'Brien Trophy in his car when he left the arena.

As for the specs, Joopiter noted that the Ferrari has a "Tipo F133A 5.5-litre naturally aspirated V12, producing 485 horsepower through a six-speed gated manual, with a top speed of 199 mph."

Ferrari made only 3,083 550 Maranello between 1996 and 2001. Jordan's car is different than any others, though, as it was made with a custom driver seat tracks to fit his 6'6" frame.

Nike designer Tinker Hatfield later used the vehicle as the inspiration for the Air Jordan 14.

Jordan sold the car in 2002 through Lake Forest Sportscars in Illinois, and it didn't resurface until this year.

articles.title: Knicks Face Major Karl-Anthony Towns Contract Problem as $276M Extension Hits Snag
articles.summary: Karl-Anthony Towns is coming off a strong 2025-26 NBA season, helping the New York Knicks win the championship. Following that, Towns is open to accepting a...
articles.body:
Karl-Anthony Towns is coming off a strong 2025-26 NBA season, helping the New York Knicks win the championship. Following that, Towns is open to accepting a pay cut to stay in New York and help the franchise contend for another title. However, he has struggled to agree to a deal with the front office.

Towns will enter the third year of his four-year, $224 million contract extension he signed when he was with the Minnesota Timberwolves . KAT is eligible to sign a four-year, $276 million extension with the Knicks. However, reports say New York wants him to accept a four-year, $200 million deal.

So far, talks about his contract negotiations have stalled. ESPN's Malike Andrews spoke about Towns' situation on Tuesday's "NBA Today."

" Karl-Anthony Towns , from what I have been told, is willing, similarly to what Jalen Brunson did. The numbers aren't the same, but he is also willing to take a pay cut," Andrews said .

"However, the pay cut the Knicks are asking him to take, he views as unreasonable."

Karl-Anthony Towns had an uneasy Media Day on Monday. He reiterated his desire to stay in New York and wants to get the contract negotiations done.

"I mean, I've made it known," Towns said . "You know, I wanna play here. Been a fan since I was young, and so I would like to get one done, of course. That's obvious, you know? I would like to get it done so I can step on the court and feel [as] comfortable as possible."

Even his teammate, Josh Hart , has not reached an agreement for a contract extension with the Knicks. Hart is eligible to sign a $132 million contract extension.

Karl-Anthony Towns Lost Weight During the Offseason

Karl-Anthony Towns was welcomed on Media Day with a new physical look. Towns was slimmer compared to the previous year, which was something the media asked him about. According to the one-time champion, he always loses weight over the summer.

"I thought my wife thought I looked good. So I thought I was looking alright," he said. "Just, in the offseason I always lose a lot of weight."

KAT said he allows his body to recover and rest, especially after the intense playoff run the Knicks had last season. Towns played heavy minutes during New York's postseason run and had to physically battle against some of the best big men in the NBA, including San Antonio Spurs star Victor Wembanyama .

articles.title: Former Rumble Ponies break Mets rookie records
articles.summary: QUEENS, N.Y. (WIVT/WBGH) – Former Rumble Ponies AJ Ewing and Carson Benge had stellar rookie seasons. AJ Ewing started this season with the Ponies before get...
articles.body:
QUEENS, N.Y. (WIVT/WBGH) – Former Rumble Ponies AJ Ewing and Carson Benge had stellar rookie seasons.

AJ Ewing started this season with the Ponies before getting promoted to Triple-A Syracuse, where he played 12 games before getting the call in May to the big leagues.

Ewing hit 11 homers and recorded 25 stolen bases, which broke the Mets franchise record for stolen bases by a rookie. The previous record was 24 set by Mookie Wilson in 1981.

Carson Benge played for the Ponies during the 2025 season before the team went on to win the Eastern League Championship. Benge hit 20 homers and recorded 22 stolen bases, making him the first player in Mets franchise history to achieve a 20/20 rookie season. He also set the franchise rookie record for hits with 168.

History in Queens was made by these 2 players who came through Rumbletown.

articles.body:
Orlando Magic forward Tristan da Silva is already standing out to new head coach Sean Sweeney through the opening days of training camp ahead of the 2026-27 NBA season.

As the Magic wrapped up their second day of training camp , Sweeney singled out da Silva while discussing the team's progress learning his offensive system. In a video shared by Ryan Kaminski of Orlando Magic on SI NBA, Sweeney praised the third-year forward's positioning and communication during Wednesday's practice.

"We wanted to do a great job this morning with understanding some of the actions we're using and really executing on our spacing," Sweeney said. "Spacing for me is like giving respect to your teammate and having the discipline to do it every time. It's not a choice, it's not optional and so I think those guys, the players did a really good job of that today."

Da Silva was one of the players who particularly caught Sweeney's attention.

"Tristan did a really good job, just of the guys who stood out in terms of being in the right spot and then communicating," Sweeney said. "We talk a lot about communicating on defense but you want to communicate on offense as well, and he did a really good job of that."

Tristan da Silva looking to build on strong second season with Magic

Da Silva's early impression comes as the 25-year-old prepares for his third NBA season and his first playing under Sweeney.

The forward established himself as a consistent member of Orlando's rotation during the 2025-26 campaign. Da Silva averaged 9.9 points, 3.7 rebounds and 1.6 assists across 77 appearances, including 34 starts. He shot 45% from the field and 37.4% from 3-point range while averaging 24.7 minutes per game.

His perimeter shooting and ability to contribute without dominating the ball could make him particularly useful within Sweeney's offensive approach.

Sweeney has emphasized spacing throughout the opening stages of training camp , explaining that he wants the Magic to use the length and width of the floor to force defenses to cover more space. That philosophy places additional importance on players consistently maintaining their positioning and communicating with teammates.

Da Silva's early execution in those areas has already earned recognition from Orlando's new coach.

With several weeks remaining before the regular season begins, da Silva will look to continue building on that strong start as he competes for a significant role in Sweeney's rotation.

articles.title: Wolves' Chris Finch Calls Out Flopping, Hopeful NBA 'Cleans Up This Crap' During 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: Minnesota Timberwolves head coach Chris Finch made his opinion on flopping perfectly clear heading into the 2026-27 season.
articles.body:
Minnesota Timberwolves head coach Chris Finch made his opinion on flopping perfectly clear heading into the 2026-27 season.

"Hopefully the league cleans up this crap, because nobody wants to watch it," Finch said Wednesday, per Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic. "That's what they said was the feedback from the fans. They're tired of watching the flopping. And we know that it's been rewarded at too high a level, so just stop rewarding the flopping."

Krawczynski noted the league is focused on reducing flopping this season by reviewing plays after games and potentially issuing fines when needed. What's more, officials are being tasked with making more calls during the games, such as issuing technical fouls for flopping.

Notably, such a technical foul would not count toward a player's two that would lead to an ejection.

"The league made clear that the Competition Committee drew a line between flopping on non-calls and embellishing contact, saying it would not punish embellishments such as head snaps," Krawczynski explained.

"They said they're going to be more aggressive in calling technicals against flopping or fining after the fact," Finch said. "For me it's a simple fix. Just don't reward these non-basketball actions. That's it. Those of us who have been in the sport long enough know what it is and what it isn't."

Minnesota was seventh in the league in free-throw attempts per game last season even though, in the words of Finch, "We don't teach flopping here."

Perhaps with the league cracking down on flopping this season, the Timberwolves will climb even higher in those ratings as other teams that have relied on the practice see their free-throw attempts drop.

Finch will surely be paying attention to the issue when Minnesota starts its season on Oct. 21 against the Miami Heat.
